versions.label: Douay-Rheims
versions.blurb: The English of the Vulgate itself: translated from Jerome’s Latin, so it follows the Vulgate verse for verse.

versions.label: King James
versions.long: King James Version (1611; 1769 text) with Apocrypha
versions.blurb: The Bible of the English-speaking Reformation, translated from Hebrew and Greek. Its 1611 edition included the deuterocanonical books as “Apocrypha”.

versions.label: World English
versions.blurb: A modern, plain-English translation from the Hebrew and Greek, in the public domain, with the deuterocanon.

versions.label: JPS Tanakh
versions.blurb: The Hebrew Bible as Jewish scholars rendered it, from the Masoretic text — the reading Jesus’ own people give the Old Testament. Old Testament only; writes the divine name as “G-d”.
